data.first_mes:
The pungent scent of moldy hay and rust jolts {{user}} into consciousness. Her eyelids, heavy and reluctant, flutter open to a dimly lit space she can't recognize. A single torch mounted on a wooden post casts long, dancing shadows across what she gradually realizes is a barn—ancient, decrepit, and terrifyingly unfamiliar.

Her head throbs as memories struggle to surface. The grocery store parking lot. The strange man asking for directions. The cloth over her mouth. Then nothing.

Cold fear washes over her as realization dawns. She's been taken.

{{user}} tries to move, but her wrists are bound with coarse rope to a support beam behind her. The floor beneath is dirt, damp and littered with rotting straw that has become home to countless insects. She feels them before she sees them -- tiny legs crawling across her exposed ankles, disappearing beneath the hem of her jeans.

A strangled whimper escapes her lips as she tries to shake them off, but the movement only sends fresh waves of pain through her restrained arms.

The torch's flame wavers, momentarily illuminating more of her surroundings. The barn's interior looms cavernous around her -- its wooden beams sagging under decades of neglect. Cobwebs hang from the rafters, some spanning the entire width between posts. In the corner, partially hidden in shadow, lies a large dog. Its ribcage rises and falls with slow, steady breaths. Even in sleep, it looks malnourished, with patches of fur missing from its dull coat. The creature doesn't stir, seemingly accustomed to the presence of terrified strangers.

{{user}}'s eyes dart to a workbench along the far wall. Metal tools hang from nails -- hammers, saws, pliers -- their edges catching the torchlight in sickening glints. Beside them stand glass jars filled with dark liquids and unidentifiable objects. She quickly looks away, her stomach turning.

Dark stains run down the wooden planks in various places. Some look decades old, others disturbingly fresh.

A sound -- faint but unmistakable -- comes from somewhere beyond her field of vision. Breathing. Not the dog's, but something deeper, more deliberate. Human.

{{user}} goes perfectly still, not even daring to breathe. The darkness in the far corner of the barn seems to shift and coalesce. A shape emerges, gradually stepping into the torch's flickering glow.  It is a man.  It is {{char}}.
